exchanges.name: Saudi Exchange
exchanges.blurb: The Arab world’s largest exchange by market value, dominated by Aramco. Trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.

exchanges.name: Borsa İstanbul
exchanges.blurb: Türkiye’s only exchange. Priced in lira, so its index level carries the country’s inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.

exchanges.name: Dubai Financial Market
exchanges.blurb: The Gulf’s main listing venue for property and banking. Moved from a Sunday–Thursday week to Monday–Friday in 2022, unlike Riyadh.

exchanges.name: Bursa Malaysia
exchanges.blurb: The world’s largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.

exchanges.name: Indonesia Stock Exchange
exchanges.blurb: The exchange of the world’s largest Muslim-majority country, heavily weighted to commodities and banking.

exchanges.name: Tokyo Stock Exchange
exchanges.blurb: Asia’s largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.

exchanges.name: Hong Kong Stock Exchange
exchanges.blurb: Where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital — the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.

exchanges.name: Shanghai Stock Exchange
exchanges.blurb: Mainland China’s main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.

exchanges.name: Korea Exchange
exchanges.blurb: Dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix — a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.

exchanges.name: Bombay Stock Exchange
exchanges.blurb: Asia’s oldest exchange, founded 1875, and the benchmark for Indian equities.

exchanges.name: Singapore Exchange
exchanges.blurb: Southeast Asia’s financial hub, weighted to banks and regional property.

exchanges.name: Taiwan Stock Exchange
exchanges.blurb: TSMC alone is roughly a third of the index, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.

exchanges.name: Stock Exchange of Thailand
exchanges.blurb: Thailand’s benchmark, sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.

exchanges.name: Philippine Stock Exchange
exchanges.blurb: A small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.

exchanges.name: Australian Securities Exchange
exchanges.blurb: Mining and banking. Often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.

exchanges.name: Johannesburg Stock Exchange
exchanges.blurb: Africa’s largest exchange by far, and the continent’s only one with a usable public daily series.

exchanges.name: B3
exchanges.blurb: Latin America’s largest exchange, driven by iron ore, oil and Brazilian rates.

exchanges.name: Bolsa Mexicana de Valores
exchanges.blurb: Mexico’s benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.

exchanges.name: Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos
exchanges.blurb: Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years. Direction over a day means something; the level does not.

exchanges.name: Toronto Stock Exchange
exchanges.blurb: Energy, mining and banks — a commodity index wearing an equity index’s clothes.

exchanges.name: New York Stock Exchange
exchanges.blurb: The largest equity market on earth. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.

exchanges.name: London Stock Exchange
exchanges.blurb: Most FTSE 100 revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.

exchanges.name: Deutsche Börse
exchanges.blurb: Germany’s industrial and chemical base — Europe’s clearest export barometer.

exchanges.name: Euronext Paris
exchanges.blurb: Luxury goods and energy dominate — unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.

exchanges.name: Euronext Amsterdam
exchanges.blurb: The world’s oldest exchange, now carried largely by ASML.

exchanges.name: Bolsa de Madrid
exchanges.blurb: Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.

exchanges.name: Borsa Italiana
exchanges.blurb: Banks and utilities, and the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.

exchanges.name: SIX Swiss Exchange
exchanges.blurb: Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.

exchanges.name: Nasdaq Stockholm
exchanges.blurb: Nordic industrials and telecoms, and a useful early read on European capital spending.

exchanges.name: Tel Aviv Stock Exchange
exchanges.blurb: Trades Sunday to Thursday. Heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
